description:
AGRIBALYSE 3.2 ships 201 land occupation and transformation rows, written in ecoinvent 3's land vocabulary because the underlying inventories are ecoinvent's -- 178 under `Resources / land`, 15 under the bare `Resources` heading, and 8 misfiled among the ground, water and biotic resources. A land row carries no registry number, so the merge looks its class up in `land-flow-classes.json` by the row's own identifier, and no AGRIBALYSE identifier was in that file: on the first build to merge the list (1 September 2026, `b0b8d76`), 69 rows reached an existing class flow by label matching and the other 132 minted 120 new published flows -- title-cased copies of classes the list already publishes, one of them a `Transformation, To Annual Crop` filed as a ground resource.

#849 adds the 201 rows to the curated table. 199 decompose onto the existing axes; the two vineyard rows state a crop the axes had no word for, so `crop_type` gains `vine` beside `fruit` rather than coarsening what the vendor said. Four names carry a country the way BAFU's rail rows do (`Occupation, annual crop, CN`), and the geography splitter's whitelist gains those four base labels so the place comes off the name (#65) and the class is the sibling's. The folds this produces -- the bare-heading duplicates, the country spellings, the misfiled compartment copies, all landing on one class flow -- are recorded in `land-flow-groupings.json`, seventeen new groupings beside the two the registration already carried.

Marked pending until a shared build merges agribalyse-3.2: these claims are about that list's rows, and a build that has not merged the list cannot grade them. Drop the flag in the change that records the first shared build made from a commit containing both #355 and this fix.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's `Transformation, from annual crop` reaches the published From cropland flow by its curated class
expectations.comment: The busiest unmatched row in the whole list: 4,390 of AGRIBALYSE's 20,440 processes exchange it. On the build of 1 September 2026 it minted `Transformation, From Annual Crop` (a title-cased duplicate of this flow) instead of matching; the class table now says what it is and the merge reads the table before it reads names.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's `Transformation, to annual crop` reaches the published To cropland flow by its curated class
expectations.comment: The second-busiest row, 4,365 processes. Same shape as its `from` twin above.

expectations.title: No published flow carries AGRIBALYSE's title-cased spelling of the annual-crop transformation
expectations.comment: The duplicate itself, named the way the build of 1 September 2026 published it. What has to stop is a vendor's spelling standing as a published flow name beside the class flow the list already had -- the same claim 0810 makes for Stepwise's spellings.

expectations.title: `Occupation, annual crop, CN` sheds its country and reaches the Cropland flow its sibling reaches
expectations.comment: The place is split off the name (#65) and recorded as the row's location; where the crop grew is not a land class. The fold onto the sibling's flow is recorded in land-flow-groupings.json.

expectations.title: The `Occupation, annual crop` filed under biotic resources reaches Cropland like its land-compartment siblings
expectations.comment: The class is keyed to the row's identifier, not its compartment, which is how BAFU's 29 land rows outside `resources / land` already reach their classes. On the build of 1 September 2026 this row minted a Cropland copy in the biotic resource context.

expectations.title: The vineyard occupation is published as its own class rather than coarsened to bare permanent cropland
expectations.comment: `Occupation, permanent crop, vine` states a crop type the axes had no word for; `crop_type` gains `vine` beside `fruit` so the vendor's statement is kept rather than dropped. A new class is the right mint -- what #351 retires is duplicates of classes the list already had.
